test.name: Record-to-person attribution should not trigger timeline
test.description: User asks whether an unlinked 1850 census record (src_001, a clean match on every identifier) is the same person as the subject. That's person-evidence (scoring the match and creating the person_evidence link), not timeline. Timeline arranges events chronologically; it does not decide record-to-person attribution. Uses flynn-record-matching, where person_evidence is empty and no conflict/hypothesis is already logged for this record, so the attribution decision is still genuinely open (mid-research-flynn's death certificate is unsuitable here — its person_evidence link, pe_005, is already made). src_001 (the clean match) is used rather than src_003 (the 'Flinn' surname-variant record) because the variant's genuine matching uncertainty pulls routing toward conflict-resolution's identity-conflict machinery instead — a real, separate boundary question, not this test's target.

input.user_message: The 1850 census (src_001) lists a Patrick Flynn, age 5, in Thomas Flynn's household — matching my Patrick Flynn on every identifier. Is this the same person? Evaluate the match and link it.

negative.explanation: The user is asking whether an unlinked record's persona is the same individual as the subject — a record-to-person attribution decision. That is person-evidence's job (scoring the match, creating/weighing person_evidence links). Timeline can reveal that records don't cohere, but it does not perform this attribution decision.

judge_context: Should route to person-evidence (record-to-person attribution and linking), not build or regenerate a timeline
